chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Samaan, who said:

I asked him about the skins of wild beasts, whether one may derive benefit from them, so he said: 'If you slaughter it and recite the name [of God], then benefit from its skin; as for the dead animal [beast of prey], then [do not benefit from it].'

key_terms.السِّبَاعِ: Wild beasts or animals of prey
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةُ: The dead animal [specifically referring to the prey type in this context]
key_terms.رَمَيْتَهُ: You threw [the dart/weapon] at it [indicating the act of hunting/slaughtering]

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using the skin of a wild animal if it is hunted but not properly slaughtered?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between hunted wild beasts and other dead animals regarding the purity of their skins. It establishes that reciting God's name during the act of killing renders the skin pure and usable, whereas a mere 'dead animal' without this ritual slaughter remains impure. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the method of death in determining the ritual status of animal by-products.
